brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A powder of dehydrated tea flavour, aroma and colour compounds that turns into a cup of tea when water is added. Sugar, citric acid or flavours such as lemon or raspberry are often included.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: The earliest form dates to 1885 in the United Kingdom, when a patent covered a paste of concentrated tea extract, sugar and evaporated milk. Little progress followed until spray drying made it possible to dry tea concentrate without harming its flavour.
processing: Tea concentrate is dried to a powder, typically by spray drying, at a temperature that spares its flavour.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Expect what black teas usually give: malty, sweet and brisk.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
